honest_conclusion: Antigravity's native run_command delivers genuine completion-triggered notifications for commands <600s (task-1290, 3s, exit 0), but enforces a hard 600s wall-clock kill even on backgrounded commands (task-1226, killed at 600s). Therefore, Antigravity does NOT support native >600s completion-triggered background execution; it falls under KS-07 Transition 3 (unsupported-host cap for >600s native completion). Detached OS execution (outer-launch.py, pid=37143, 605.04s, os_exit_code=0) survives >600s, while schedule(DurationSeconds=620) is strictly a fixed-time reminder and is NOT claimed to be a completion-triggered notification. U7 remains uncredited until run 2 on a host whose native background execution survives >600s.
